observations: Fix3 (_is_protocol_only_prefix) correctly rejects scheme+authority-only prefixes (https://, http://, https://a.com) while allowing prefixes with path delimiters (https://a.com/, https://example.com/)

All 5 parent established conditions (P1/G1/G2/G3/G5) survive with binding_accuracy=1.0 and slot_count=1, confirming Fix3 does not regress path-prefix, query-string, deep-path, or hybrid parameterization
Null controls N1_ORIGINAL and N1_CORRECTED maintain slot_count=0 (Fix2 and empty-prefix guard still effective)
PROTOCOL_ONLY condition (Fix3 primary target) now produces slot_count=0, resolving the protocol-only gap from parent handoff
B_UNFIXED_PROTOCOL_ONLY baseline produces slot_count=1 (over-parameterized https://${url}), confirming Fix3 necessity: without Fix3, protocol-only URLs produce false parameterization
B_UNFIXED_G1 baseline produces binding_accuracy=0.0 (suffix-corrupted template ${url}a), confirming Fix1 necessity inherited from parent
B_LITERAL baseline produces fail_rate=1.0 (confidence 0.5 < min_confidence 0.8), confirming parameterized induction necessary
Template invariance preserved: slot_prefixes extraction is metadata-only, action_template matches parent for all parameterized conditions
Realistic corpus: 4/6 conditions parameterize correctly (R1 REST API, R3 CDN deep path, R5 minimal prefix with path delimiter, R4 fails Fix2 boundary)
R2_QUERY_HEAVY fails binding (template varies only q param, unseen values lack page param) — test design issue, not algorithm failure

R6_PROTOCOL_ONLY_SHALLOW parameterizes (slot_count=1) because https://a.com/ has a path delimiter, unlike pure protocol-only https://a.com — spec expected slot_count=0 but this is consistent with Fix3 definition
All 10 decision-rule conditions pass: verdict SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST
validity_notes: All conditions are deterministic synthetic with zero model/network/browser calls — no external validity for real-browser traffic
Fix3 implementation uses structural check (scheme+authority delimiter presence) rather than raw prefix length threshold, which is more robust than the originally proposed 12-char threshold
R2_QUERY_HEAVY expected URLs in test spec are inconsistent with the parameterization algorithm (unseen values should include &page= parameter)
R4_CROSS_PROTOCOL fails because Fix2 rejects prefix ending at non-delimiter character (version segment 'v') — this is a Fix2 limitation for path-embedded parameters, not a Fix3 issue
R6_PROTOCOL_ONLY_SHALLOW was expected slot_count=0 in spec but correctly parameterizes with Fix3 — the spec conflated domain length with protocol-only classification
Realistic corpus is synthetic approximation, not real API traffic — prevalence measurement is illustrative only
n=3 training + 3 unseen per condition establishes determinism on synthetic data, not statistical generalization
B_UNFIXED_G1 and B_UNFIXED_PROTOCOL_ONLY baselines are reported for fix necessity quantification but not gated by decision rule
unresolved: Fix2 limitation: path-embedded version parameters (e.g., /v1/data vs /v2/data) fail Fix2 boundary check because prefix ends at non-delimiter character. Requires domain-aware or segment-aware prefix validation for versioned API patterns.
